chunks: He, peace be upon him, was asked about a pond in which there is a carcass.
So he said: "If the water overpowers it, such that no odor is found from it, then perform wudu (ablution) and ghusl with it."

key_terms.الرِّيحُ: the odor or smell indicating contamination
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the water being assessed for purity
key_terms.جِيفَةٌ: a carcass or dead animal body
key_terms.غَدِيرٍ: a pond or small body of standing water

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) and ghusl be performed with pond water that contains a dead animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the purity of pond water in which a carcass is present. If the water remains dominant and no odor from the carcass is detectable, it may still be used for wudu (ablution) and ghusl.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.22 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a pond with a dead animal in it.
Imam (as) said: "If the water overpowers it so that no odor is detectable, then perform ablution and ghusl with it”.
